Full summary: Wrote and self-reviewed the dashboard scale redesign spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-09-dashboard-scale-design.md) — Approach B approved by Dave: server query layer + compact client index, canvas density timeline, drill-down graph explorer, virtualized faceted lists, health panel, scope breadcrumb, hash routing.
Decisions: Chose client-side compact index (~200KB gzipped at 5k+5k, delta polling via since param with count-mismatch full refetch) over fully server-windowed queries — buys instant facets, scope rollups, and timeline bucketing at the confirmed 5k envelope; invalidated above ~20-30k records per store, API shape leaves room to move windowing server-side later.; Chose to keep vanilla JS split into native ES modules over adding a build step — the hard parts (canvas timeline, data contract) gain nothing from a framework and a toolchain adds weight to a zero-config npm package.; Chose to delete vis-timeline but retain cytoscape — vis-timeline's core idiom is per-item DOM and cannot aggregate; cytoscape is fine when capped at ~200 elements in ego/overview views.; Chose Health as a section in the Insights tab over an 8th tab — cards deep-link into pre-filtered views so it is a router, not a destination.; Added .playwright-mcp/ to .gitignore — Playwright MCP writes snapshots/screenshots into the repo root during browser-driven UI development.
Findings: Spec has one explicit implementation-time decision point (section 1.1): how decision status changes surface in delta polling — filter on updated_at if the store tracks it, else rely on count-mismatch full refetch; criterion documented in spec.; Suggested phasing in spec section 11: (1) server query layer + index store + 5k seed fixture, (2) shared virtualized list, (3) density timeline, (4) graph drill-down, (5) health + scope breadcrumb + hash routing + scale verification.
